content: ALX homeobox protein 1 is a protein encoded by the ALX1 gene in humans. The precise function of the ALX1 gene in humans has not yet been fully elucidated. However, in rodent models, this gene is essential for the survival of the forebrain mesenchyme. It may also play a role in the development of the cervix. Mutations in the ALX1 gene in mice have been associated with neural tube defects, including acrania (absence of the cranial vault) and meroanencephaly (partial absence of the brain). In Darwin's finches, which inhabit the Galapagos Islands, the ALX1 gene has been implicated in the variation of beak shapes, contributing to their adaptive evolution. The ALX1 protein has been demonstrated to interact with Importin-13 (IPO13), a nuclear transport protein.
